props.title: Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan

sections.content: **Danger Close: The Battle of Long Tan (2019)** (2019) stands among the most intense modern Vietnam War films, depicting the true story of 108 inexperienced Australian and New Zealand soldiers who faced off against 2,500 Viet Cong fighters. It follows in the tradition of visceral combat films like **Black Hawk Down** (2001) and We Were Soldiers (2002), but brings a uniquely Australian perspective rarely seen in Vietnam War cinema. Director Kriv Stenders captures the claustrophobic tension of soldiers trapped in a rubber plantation during a monsoon, creating a sense of desperate isolation that recalls **The Siege of Jadotville** (2016).

sections.content: What sets **Danger Close** apart is its focus on the ANZAC (Australian and New Zealand Army Corps) experience, continuing a tradition of Australian war films like **Breaker Morant** (1980) and **Gallipoli** (1981). The film meticulously recreates the August 1966 battle with attention to period detail, while Travis Fimmel's performance as Major Harry Smith captures the weight of command similar to Tom Hanks in **Saving Private Ryan** (1998).

The technical achievement in sound design and practical effects rivals recent war films like **Dunkirk** (2017) and **1917** (2019). The film's approach to combat sequences emphasizes confusion and chaos rather than glorification, drawing parallels to the documentary-like style of **The Battle of Long Tan** (2006) and **Fog of War** (2003). sections.content: **Danger Close** represents a new wave of war films that prioritize historical accuracy and psychological realism over Hollywood spectacle, similar to **Hacksaw Ridge** (2016) and **13 Hours** (2016). The film's portrayal of young soldiers thrust into combat echoes themes found in **Full Metal Jacket** (1987), while its focus on a single battle draws comparison to **Black Hawk Down** (2001).
